newsitem.title: PANAMA: Philippines president Ramos starts Panama visit.
newsitem.headline: Philippines president Ramos starts Panama visit.

text.p: Philippines President Fidel Ramos arrived in Panama on Tuesday for an official visit intended to boost economic ties between the two Pacific Rim nations.
Panama is keen to broaden ties with countries that belong to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum and will use Ramos' two-day visit to that end, government officials said.
The APEC groups 18 nations representing the Asian Pacific Rim plus Canada, Chile, Mexico and the United States.

"This is the first time an Asian leader has visited Panama and for the first time Panama will be able to talk about APEC with a member," Foreign Ministry top official Marcel Salamin told local RPC radio.

Noting that Asian countries already widely use the Panama Canal and free-trade zone, he predicted that Panama would in the future be "more important as a trans-shipment point for the Western Hemisphere" with the recent partial privatisation of its two main ports and only railroad.

Panama is also expected to propose a regional distribution centre for Pacific Rim countries during the Philippine leader's visit. The centre would be a type of free-trade zone for APEC countries to distribute their products to Latin America from Panama, a Commerce Ministry spokesman said.

Ramos, who arrived from Mexico accompanied by a 200-person delegation including some 60 businessmen, was due to meet with President Ernesto Perez Balladares on Tuesday afternoon. The Panamanian leader visited the Philippines in 1995.
Ramos was also scheduled to discuss investment opportunities in U.S. military installations that are scheduled to be turned over to Panamanian control in 1999.
